samasa.meaning: a gāyatrī short of a syllable

translation.literal: Of the Sāvitrī: the seer Viśvāmitra; nicṛd-gāyatrī the metre; Savitṛ the deity; the use in the Gāyatrī japa.
translation.readable: The Gāyatrī: seer Viśvāmitra, metre nicṛd-gāyatrī, deity Savitṛ; used for the japa.

meaning: A viniyoga is the statement said before a mantra of its seer (ṛṣi), its metre (chandas), its deity (devatā) and the use (viniyoga) it is put to. Here: the Gāyatrī itself, called Sāvitrī after its deity, before the japa. The metre is given as nicṛd-gāyatrī, ‘a gāyatrī wanting one syllable’: as written, the verse has twenty-three syllables, one short of the twenty-four of the gāyatrī (the first pāda is counted full by reading vareṇiyam).
in_the_rite: Step nyasa, before the nyāsas and the meditation, in all three services.
